key_insight: RASGD replaces per-arrival re-solving with a single stochastic-gradient price update that stays feasible online and achieves logarithmic regret.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable, low-memory alternative for large LLM inference and search systems that must allocate scarce resources in real time.
method: Update dual resource prices from each arriving request and current inventory.
Use an adaptive stepsize that is smaller early and larger later to match inventory dynamics.
Avoid LP re-solving and sample-average optimization, keeping per-arrival work at O(m) for m resources.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports O(log T) expected regret versus realized fractional hindsight optimum, feasibility on every sample path, and numerical experiments showing competitiveness with LP re-solving and better performance than first-order baselines.
watch_item: The guarantee relies on standard non-degeneracy assumptions, so performance may degrade or require care when those conditions are violated in practice.
paper_title: Resource-Adaptive Stochastic Gradient Descent for Online Linear Programming without Re-solving
